mainTopic: Miscarriage claims in the ten-year rule, whether a woman is commanded in פריה ורביה, and teachings on rebuke and peace
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of a couple married ten years without children. In two cases the wife is believed, because her claim gives her a worse status: she would not falsely call herself an עקרה, or falsely claim three miscarriages. Then a new משנה teaches that only the man is commanded in פריה ורביה, while רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says both are commanded. The גמרא learns the first view from "וכבשוה", which is spelled as singular, and רב יוסף learns it from the singular "פרה ורבה" said to יעקב. Next the גמרא gathers more teachings of רבי אילעא: hold back rebuke that will not be heard, and you may change the facts for the sake of peace, as even הקדוש ברוך הוא did. Back on the משנה, רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי argue whether the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, and a story about רבי אמי and רבי אסי shows that רבי יוחנן ruled against him. A ruling of רבי יוחנן ordering a divorce with כתובה is pushed aside, since a woman can claim she needs children to care for her in old age. The amud ends with the story of יהודית, wife of רבי חייא, and that story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: He says she miscarried, she says she did not: she is believed
steps.stepSummary: The husband claims his wife miscarried within the ten years, so the count should restart. She denies it. רבי אמי rules that she is believed, because no woman would falsely make herself out to be an עקרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The husband said: 'You miscarried within the ten years.' The wife said: 'I did not miscarry.' רבי אמי said: Even here she is believed, because if she really had miscarried, she would not label herself as barren.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a case where husband and wife argue about whether she miscarried, and רבי אמי rules that her word is accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she miscarried, the ten years are counted again from the miscarriage, so he would not yet have to divorce her. By denying it, she is calling herself an עקרה, which is a bad status for her. A person does not lie in order to give herself a bad name, so we trust her.

keyTerms.meaning: She would not set herself up (in a certain status)

phrases.english: He said: You miscarried within the ten [years].
phrases.notes: If she miscarried, the ten years start over, so he wouldn't have to divorce her yet.

phrases.english: And she said: I did not miscarry.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: אַף בְּזוֹ הִיא נֶאֱמֶנֶת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said: Even in this case she is believed.
For if it were true that she miscarried,
she would not establish herself as a barren woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: אַף בְּזוֹ הִיא נֶאֱמֶנֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (before this section) of the ten-year rule and miscarriages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the husband claims a miscarriage and the wife denies it, the wife is believed, since she would not falsely call herself an עקרה.

steps.title: Three miscarriages create a set status
steps.stepSummary: A woman who miscarried three times has a חזקה of being a woman who miscarries.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she miscarried, then miscarried again, and then miscarried again, she is established as a woman who miscarries.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule: three miscarriages give the woman a fixed status of one who miscarries. This rule sets up the argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One or two miscarriages could be chance, but three create a חזקה, a pattern we rely on. With that status she is treated like a woman who will not bear living children, so the husband must divorce her to fulfill פריה ורביה with someone else.

phrases.english: If she miscarried, and miscarried again,
and miscarried yet again,
she is established as one who miscarries.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִפִּילָה, וְחָזְרָה וְהִפִּילָה, וְחָזְרָה וְהִפִּילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from one disputed miscarriage to the rule about a pattern of three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three miscarriages establish a חזקה that she is a woman who miscarries.

steps.title: He says two miscarriages, she says three: she is believed
steps.stepSummary: The husband says she miscarried twice, and she says three times. רבי יצחק בן אלעזר reports a case in the בית מדרש where they ruled that she is believed, because she would not falsely give herself the status of one who miscarries.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said she miscarried twice; she said three times. רבי יצחק בן אלעזר said: This exact case came up in the study hall, and they said she is believed, because if she had not miscarried a third time, she would not set herself up as a woman who miscarries.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the same reasoning as step 1 to the three-miscarriage rule, using a real case decided in the בית מדרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two miscarriages there is no חזקה yet, but with three there is. Her claim of three gives her a bad status, so it is against her own interest, and we believe her for the same reason as in step 1.
steps.whatToRemember: In both cases the wife is believed for the same reason: a woman would not lie in a way that gives her a worse status (עקרה or one who miscarries).

phrases.english: He said: She miscarried twice,
and she said: Three times.
Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar said:
There was such a case in the study hall,
and they said: She is believed,
for if it were true that she did not miscarry [a third time],
she would not establish herself as one who miscarries.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹבָדָא הֲוָה בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא, וַאֲמַרוּ: הִיא מְהֵימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reasoning of step 1 to the rule of step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When he says two miscarriages and she says three, she is believed, since she would not falsely create a חזקה of miscarrying for herself.

steps.title: The משנה: only the man is commanded to have children
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens: the man is commanded in פריה ורביה, but the woman is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A man is commanded in the מצוה of having children, but a woman is not.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with the opinion of the תנא קמא: the obligation of פריה ורביה falls on the man only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a basic rule about who carries the מצוה. It explains why, in the earlier cases, the husband is the one pushed to divorce in order to have children. The source for the rule is not given here; the גמרא will ask for it.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה to be fruitful and multiply (have children)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הָאִישׁ מְצֻוֶּוה עַל פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה,
phrases.english: MISHNAH: A man is commanded regarding being fruitful and multiplying,
but not a woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאִישׁ מְצֻוֶּוה עַל פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, moving from the miscarriage cases to the basic question of who is commanded.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The man is obligated in פריה ורביה; the woman is not.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה: both are commanded
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה disagrees and says the woman is also commanded, because the פסוק "פרו ורבו" is said to both of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says: About both of them the Torah says, 'And God blessed them, and God said to them: Be fruitful and multiply.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a dissenting view: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה holds that both man and woman are commanded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof is the plural wording: "אותם" (them) and "להם" (to them), meaning אדם and חוה together. So the command was spoken to both.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says:
About both of them it says:
"And God blessed them,
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:28

phrases.english: and God said to them: Be fruitful and multiply."
phrases.notes: Some versions add the word in square brackets, so it matches the פסוק exactly.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר: עַל שְׁנֵיהֶם הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא of step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman is also commanded in פריה ורביה, since the פסוק addresses both.

steps.title: The גמרא asks for the source that a woman is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the תנא קמא learns that only the man is commanded.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the תנא קמא's rule. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain פסוק seems to speak to both, as רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה argued. So the תנא קמא needs a reason from the text to exempt the woman.

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He means: how do we know a woman is not commanded, as the first opinion in the משנה said?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the תנא קמא's ruling in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that a woman is not obligated in פריה ורביה.

steps.title: "And conquer it": the command is aimed at the man
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון answers from the end of the same פסוק, "ומלאו את הארץ וכבשוה". Conquering is a man's way, not a woman's, so the command is addressed to the man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: The פסוק says, 'Fill the land and conquer it.' It is a man's way to conquer, and it is not a woman's way to conquer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the word "וכבשוה" (conquer it) shows that the whole command is directed at men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Fill the land" and "conquer it" are part of the same command as "פרו ורבו". Since conquering is something men do, the command as a whole is addressed to the man. So even though "להם" sounds like both, the מצוה falls on the man.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא exempts the woman from פריה ורביה because the same פסוק says "וכבשוה", and conquering is a man's way. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה reads "להם" as including both.
steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions use the same פסוק (בראשית 1:28). רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה looks at "אותם / להם"; the תנא קמא looks at "וכבשוה" at the end.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said
in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon:
The verse says: "And fill the land and conquer it."
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:28, the same פסוק as "פרו ורבו".

phrases.english: It is a man's way to conquer,
and it is not a woman's way to conquer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word "וכבשוה" in the same פסוק shows the command is directed at men, since conquering is a man's way, not a woman's.
steps.whyThisMatters: This derivation is the basis for the halacha that the מצוה of פריה ורביה belongs to the man.

steps.title: But 'And conquer it' sounds plural
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רבי אילעא's proof: the word 'וכבשוה' is plural, so it seems to speak to both man and woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary: 'And conquer it' is in the plural, so it means two people!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 7. The word 'וכבשוה' looks plural, so it seems to point to both the man and the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אילעא used 'conquer it' to show the command is aimed at the man alone. But the word looks plural, which would include the woman too. So the proof seems to work in the opposite direction and support רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the evidence points the other way

phrases.english: On the contrary:
'And conquer it' means two!
phrases.notes: The word is in the plural, like 'you all, conquer it', so it sounds like it is talking to both of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אילעא's proof from 'וכבשוה' that only the man is commanded
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word is plural, so it addresses both the man and the woman, which supports the opposite view.

steps.title: The word is spelled as singular
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the word is written without the ו, so it reads as singular.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: it is written 'וכבשה', which can be read as singular.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק defends the proof. He points out how the word is actually spelled in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We read the word aloud as plural, but it is written without the ו, so the spelling can be read as singular. That spelling hints that the conquering, and so the command, is aimed at one person, the man. The proof from step 7 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written; how the word is spelled in the תורה
And conquer it, read from the spelling as singular

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up how the word is read aloud with how it is spelled. The answer depends on the spelling, which has no ו.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
It is written 'and conquer it' (singular).
phrases.notes: The word is spelled without the ו, so the spelling can be read as talking to just one person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: וְכׇבְשֶׁהָ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural reading 'וכבשוה' includes the woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: The spelling is singular, so the command is directed at the man alone.

steps.title: A different source: 'פרה ורבה' in the singular
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings another source for the תנא קמא: the command to יעקב uses the singular 'פרה ורבה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: the source is from here: 'I am God Almighty, be fruitful and multiply' in the singular. It does not say the plural 'פרו ורבו'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a second answer to the question from step 6, using a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the command was repeated to יעקב, it was said in the singular, to one man. This shows that the command belongs to the man. This proof does not depend on how 'וכבשוה' is spelled.

keyTerms.meaning: From here; introduces a different source

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא's view that only the man is commanded has two sources: the singular spelling of 'וכבשה' (רבי אילעא with רב נחמן בר יצחק) and the singular 'פרה ורבה' said to יעקב (רב יוסף).

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: from here:
'I am God Almighty, be fruitful and multiply' (singular),
phrases.notes: בראשית 35:11

phrases.english: and it does not say 'be fruitful and multiply' (plural).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the question of step 6, in place of the 'וכבשוה' proof
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that only the man is commanded in פריה ורביה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The singular command 'פרה ורבה' said to יעקב

steps.title: Say what will be heard, hold back what won't
steps.stepSummary: Another teaching of רבי אילעא: just as it is a מצוה to say words that will be listened to, it is a מצוה not to say words that will not be listened to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: Just as it is a מצוה for a person to say something that will be listened to, so it is a מצוה for a person not to say something that will not be listened to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes more teachings from the same רבי אילעא, and this first one is about when to speak up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Correcting someone who will listen is a מצוה. Here we learn that holding back is also a מצוה when the person will not listen. Speaking up is valuable only when it can actually help.

keyTerms.meaning: Words that will be listened to and accepted

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Ile'a said in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon:
Just as it is a מצוה for a person
to say something that will be listened to —
so it is a מצוה for a person
not to say something that will not be listened to.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New teaching linked only by having the same speakers as step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is a מצוה not to say words of rebuke that will not be accepted.

steps.title: רבי אבא: holding back is an obligation
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא goes further and says that holding back is an obligation, based on the פסוק 'Do not rebuke a scorner'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא says: it is an obligation, as it says: 'Do not rebuke a scorner, or he will hate you. Rebuke a wise man, and he will love you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא makes the rule from step 11 stronger. Holding back is a must, not just a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק gives a direct command, 'do not rebuke', so holding back is required and not only praiseworthy. Rebuking a scorner only makes him hate you and achieves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A scorner; someone who mocks good advice

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba says: it is an obligation,
as it says: 'Do not rebuke a scorner lest he hate you;'
phrases.notes: משלי 9:8

phrases.english: 'rebuke a wise man and he will love you.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַבָּא אוֹמֵר: חוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the rule of step 11 from a מצוה to an obligation
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Holding back rebuke from someone who will not listen is an obligation.

steps.title: Allowed to change the truth for peace
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא teaches that a person may change the facts for the sake of peace, as יוסף's brothers did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: A person is allowed to change the facts for the sake of peace, as it says: 'Your father commanded... So shall you say to יוסף: Please forgive...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a third teaching from רבי אילעא. A person may bend the truth to keep peace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After יעקב died, the brothers told יוסף that their father had commanded him to forgive them. The פסוק brings this as a proof that changing the facts is allowed when it keeps peace. Here it is only described as allowed, not required.

keyTerms.meaning: To change; to bend the facts

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Ile'a said in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon:

phrases.aramaic: מוּתָּר לוֹ לָאָדָם לְשַׁנּוֹת בִּדְבַר הַשָּׁלוֹם,
phrases.english: A person is permitted to change the facts for the sake of peace,
as it says: 'Your father commanded, etc.
phrases.notes: בראשית 50:16. The brothers say this to יוסף, and the proof assumes יעקב never really said it.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּה תֹאמְרוּ לְיוֹסֵף אָנָּא שָׂא נָא וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: So shall you say to Joseph: Please forgive, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: מוּתָּר לוֹ לָאָדָם לְשַׁנּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of the same speakers, on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is permitted to change the facts for the sake of peace.

steps.title: רבי נתן: changing for peace is a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן says changing the facts for peace is a מצוה, learning it from what שמואל was told when he feared שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: it is a מצוה, as it says: 'And שמואל said: How can I go? If שאול hears, he will kill me...'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן goes further than step 13. Changing the facts for peace is a מצוה, not just allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13 the proof was from the brothers' own words, which only shows it is allowed. רבי נתן's proof comes from a conversation between ה׳ and שמואל. Since the instruction came from ה׳, it counts as a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: A commandment; more than just allowed

steps.whatToRemember: Two pairs of opinions: holding back rebuke is a מצוה (רבי אילעא) or an obligation (רבי אבא). Changing the facts for peace is allowed (רבי אילעא) or a מצוה (רבי נתן).

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says: it is a מצוה,
as it says: 'And Samuel said: How can I go?
Saul will hear and kill me, etc.'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 16:2. The 'etc.' points to the rest of the פסוק, where ה׳ tells him to say he came to bring a קרבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens step 13 from allowed to a מצוה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Changing the facts for the sake of peace is a מצוה.

steps.title: Even ה׳ changed words for the sake of peace
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from דבי רבי ישמעאל teaches that peace is so great that הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself changed שרה's words when He repeated them to אברהם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Peace is great, because even הקדוש ברוך הוא changed the facts for it. At first the פסוק says שרה said "my master is old." But when ה׳ told אברהם what she said, He quoted her as saying "I am old."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more source to the peace teachings from the last steps. This time the example comes from הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שרה laughed and said that אברהם was old. When ה׳ repeated it to אברהם, He said that שרה called herself old, so אברהם would not be hurt. This is the strongest support yet for the earlier teachings of רבי אילעא and רבי נתן that one may change the facts for peace.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study hall) of רבי ישמעאל

steps.whatToRemember: Changing words for the sake of peace is so valued that the גמרא shows הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself doing it with שרה's words to אברהם.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Great is peace,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שִׁינָּה בּוֹ,
phrases.english: for even the Holy One, Blessed be He, changed [the facts] for its sake,
as at first it is written: "And my master is old,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:12. These are שרה's own words about אברהם.

phrases.english: and in the end it is written: "And I am old."
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:13. This is how ה׳ retold her words to אברהם.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל תָּנָא: גָּדוֹל הַשָּׁלוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further and stronger source to the teachings of רבי אילעא and רבי נתן about changing the facts for peace.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Peace is so great that even הקדוש ברוך הוא changed שרה's words to keep peace between her and אברהם.

steps.title: Dispute over whether the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's opinion of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. It reports that רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי argued over whether the הלכה follows him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said, "רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says." It was reported that רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי argued about this. One said the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, and the other said it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by going back to a line in the משנה. It presents an argument between two אמוראים without yet telling us who held which side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה holds that women are also commanded in פרו ורבו. The question now is practical: do we rule like him? We are told one אמורא says yes and one says no, but not which is which, and that sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a dispute among אמוראים)
The practical law does not follow...

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people named יוחנן here. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה is the תנא from the משנה. רבי יוחנן (with no last name) is the later אמורא who is ruling on whether the הלכה follows him.

phrases.english: "Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says."
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה, where he says women are also commanded in פרו ורבו.

phrases.english: It was stated:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi [disagreed]:

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה,
phrases.english: One said: The halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה.
phrases.english: and one said: The halacha does not follow Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר. אִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the peace teachings and returns to the משנה's opinion of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagree over whether the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

steps.title: Proof that רבי יוחנן ruled against רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that רבי יוחנן is the one who said the הלכה does not follow רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. When רבי אבהו quoted him as saying the opposite, רבי אמי and רבי אסי turned their faces away.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can conclude that רבי יוחנן is the one who said the הלכה does not follow him. Once רבי אבהו sat and said in רבי יוחנן's name that the הלכה does follow him, and רבי אמי and רבי אסי turned their faces away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now figures out which אמורא held which side. It uses a story about how רבי יוחנן's students reacted to a report of his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי and רבי אסי were close students of רבי יוחנן. When they heard רבי אבהו say that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, they turned away, a silent sign that the report was wrong. So רבי יוחנן must have held that the הלכה does not follow him, which leaves רבי יהושע בן לוי as the one who said it does.

keyTerms.meaning: They turned their faces away (a silent sign of disagreement)

phrases.aramaic: תִּסְתַּיַּים דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הוּא דְּאָמַר אֵין הֲלָכָה:
phrases.english: Conclude that it is Rabbi Yochanan who said the halacha does not [follow him]:
for Rabbi Abahu sat
and said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: The halacha [follows him],

phrases.aramaic: וְאַהְדְּרִינְהוּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי לְאַפַּיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi turned their faces away.
phrases.notes: They were quietly showing that they did not accept this report of רבי יוחנן's view.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיַּים דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הוּא דְּאָמַר אֵין הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles which אמורא held which side in the dispute just presented.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן is the one who said the הלכה does not follow רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אמי and רבי אסי turned away when רבי אבהו quoted רבי יוחנן as ruling like רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

steps.title: Another version: רבי חייא בר אבא was the one who reported it
steps.stepSummary: Some say that the person who quoted רבי יוחנן was רבי חייא בר אבא, not רבי אבהו, and that רבי אמי and רבי אסי turned their faces away from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it was רבי חייא בר אבא who said it, and רבי אמי and רבי אסי turned their faces away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same story with a different speaker. This sets up רב פפא's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the name of the reporter changes. The students' silent reaction stays the same, so the proof about רבי יוחנן's view still works in this version too.

phrases.english: And some say:
Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַהְדְּרִינְהוּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי לְאַפַּיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi turned their faces away.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the story in step 17, with a different person quoting רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to another version, רבי חייא בר אבא quoted רבי יוחנן, and רבי אמי and רבי אסי turned away.

steps.title: רב פפא: Why stay silent if it was רבי חייא בר אבא?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the silence makes sense if the speaker was רבי אבהו, because they respected his standing with the Roman ruler. But if it was רבי חייא בר אבא, they should have openly said, "רבי יוחנן did not say that."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It makes sense according to the one who says רבי אבהו said it. Out of respect for the Roman ruler's court, they did not say anything at all to him. But according to the one who says רבי חייא בר אבא said it, they should have told him, "רבי יוחנן did not say this!"
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא questions the second version of the story. He asks why רבי אמי and רבי אסי would only hint at their disagreement instead of correcting the speaker out loud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו was closely connected to the Roman government, so openly contradicting him would have been disrespectful. That explains why they only turned their faces. רבי חייא בר אבא had no such standing, so their silence is harder to explain in the second version.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
Respect for the Roman ruler's court

steps.whyThisMatters: In both versions, רבי יוחנן's students disagreed with the report. רב פפא is only asking how they showed it, not whether רבי יוחנן ruled against רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אַמְרַהּ,
phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says Rabbi Abahu said it,
because of the honor of Caesar's court,
phrases.notes: רבי אבהו had close ties to the Roman government, so they did not want to embarrass him openly.

phrases.english: they did not say anything at all to him.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אַמְרַהּ —
phrases.english: But according to the one who says Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said it —

phrases.aramaic: לֵימְרוּ לֵיהּ: לָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי.
phrases.english: let them say to him: Rabbi Yochanan did not say this!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אַמְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the second version of the story given in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The version saying רבי חייא בר אבא was the one who quoted רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Silent disagreement fits when the speaker was רבי אבהו, whom they respected because of his ties to the Roman ruler. With רבי חייא בר אבא there was no such reason, so they should have corrected him out loud.

steps.title: What was the final outcome?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what was finally decided about this question.
steps.simpleTranslation: What came of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the final outcome was: does the הלכה follow רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה or not? This short question sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's comment was only about how רבי אמי and רבי אסי showed their disagreement. In both versions they rejected the report that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. Now the גמרא asks for the final practical ruling and looks for an actual case decided by רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: What came of it? What was decided about it?

phrases.english: What was [the outcome] about it?
phrases.notes: "It" means the question of whether the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, that a woman is commanded too.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הֲוָה עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After identifying the positions in the dispute (steps 16-19), the גמרא asks what the final practical ruling was.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the final הלכה is in the dispute: whether a woman is commanded in פריה ורביה, as רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן ordered a divorce with כתובה payment
steps.stepSummary: A case came before רבי יוחנן in קיסרי. He ruled that the husband must divorce his wife and pay her כתובה, which seems to show that a woman is commanded in פריה ורביה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אחא בר חנינא said in the name of רבי אבהו, in the name of רבי אסי: A case came before רבי יוחנן in the synagogue of Caesarea, and he said: "The husband must divorce her and pay her כתובה." If you think a woman is not commanded, why would she get a כתובה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real ruling of רבי יוחנן as proof. He forced a husband to divorce his wife and pay her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman only has the right to demand a divorce and her כתובה if she has a real claim against her husband. If she is not commanded in פריה ורביה, she seems to have no claim at all. So רבי יוחנן must hold that she is commanded, which matches רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the opening of a proof
He must divorce her and pay her כתובה
If it enters your mind, if you think

phrases.english: Come and hear,
for Rabbi Aḥa bar Ḥanina said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Asi said:
There was an incident before Rabbi Yoḥanan
in the synagogue of Caesarea,
and he said: He must divorce her and give her the כתובה.
And if you think she is not commanded,
what is the כתובה doing here?
phrases.notes: He means: why would she have any right to force a divorce and collect her money?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer to the question of step 20 through an actual ruling of רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן holds a woman is commanded in פריה ורביה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling in Caesarea that the husband must divorce her and pay the כתובה.

steps.title: Perhaps she came with a different claim
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Perhaps the woman had another valid reason for wanting children, not the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps that was a case where she came because of a different claim.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof. The divorce could be explained even if a woman is not commanded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that the only possible claim was the מצוה of פריה ורביה. The גמרא suggests she may have had a personal, practical reason to want children. That kind of claim can also force a divorce, so the case proves nothing about whether she is commanded.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps: the opening of a rejection
She came because of a claim, a different argument of her own

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that a woman is not commanded. It is only saying that this case cannot prove either side.

phrases.english: Perhaps it was where she came because of a claim.
phrases.notes: A different claim, not the מצוה. The next two stories show what kind of claim.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא בְּבָאָה מֵחֲמַת טַעֲנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 21 by reinterpreting the case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely. It does not decide the question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the only basis for her demand was the מצוה, but a personal claim could also justify the divorce.

steps.title: The woman before רבי אמי: who will care for me when I am old?
steps.stepSummary: A woman asked רבי אמי for her כתובה. He told her she was not commanded, but when she asked who would care for her in her old age, he ruled that the husband is forced to divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the woman who came before רבי אמי. She said: "Give me my כתובה!" He said: "Go, you are not commanded!" She said: "In her old age, what will become of this woman?" He said: "In a case like this, we certainly force him."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows what "a different claim" means. It backs up the rejection in step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי first turned her away because she is not commanded in פריה ורביה. Once she raised a practical need, someone to look after her when she is old, he forced the divorce. This shows that a woman's claim can work even without the מצוה.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הַהִיא דַּאֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי.
phrases.english: Like that woman who came before Rabbi Ami.
She said to him: Give me my כתובה!
He said to her: Go, you are not commanded!
She said to him: In her old age,
what will become of this woman?
phrases.notes: She is talking about herself: without children, who will take care of her?

phrases.english: He said: In a case like this, we certainly force [him].

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הַהִיא דַּאֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates and supports the rejection in step 22 by showing a real example of a valid claim.
steps.raayaObject: That a woman's practical claim, apart from the מצוה, can force a divorce with כתובה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אמי's ruling in the case of the woman worried about her old age.

steps.title: The woman before רב נחמן: a staff and a hoe
steps.stepSummary: A woman came before רב נחמן with the same kind of claim: she needed children to support her in old age and to bury her. He also ruled that the husband is forced.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman came before רב נחמן. He said: "You are not commanded." She said: "Doesn't this woman need a staff for her hand and a hoe for her burial?" He said: "In a case like this, we certainly force him."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, matching story with רב נחמן. It strengthens the point that a practical claim forces a divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי אמי, רב נחמן first said she is not commanded. Her picture of a staff to lean on and a hoe to dig her grave showed her real need for children. So he forced the divorce, confirming that the case of רבי יוחנן cannot prove that a woman is commanded.
steps.whatToRemember: Even someone who holds that a woman is not commanded in פריה ורביה agrees that she can force a divorce and get her כתובה if she needs children to care for her. So רבי יוחנן's ruling does not settle the question.

phrases.english: A certain woman came before Rav Naḥman.
He said to her: You are not commanded.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: לָא בָּעֲיָא הָךְ אִתְּתָא
phrases.english: She said to him: Doesn't this woman need
a staff for her hand and a hoe for burial?
phrases.notes: She means children to lean on when she is old and to bury her when she dies.

phrases.english: He said: In a case like this, we certainly force [him].

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא דַּאֲתַאי לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story that adds a second example to step 23.
steps.raayaObject: That a woman's need for children to support her can force a divorce, even though she is not commanded.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's ruling in the case of the woman who needed a staff and a hoe.

steps.title: Background: the twins יהודה and חזקיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives background: רבי חייא's sons יהודה and חזקיה were twins, but one was fully formed at the end of nine months and the other at the start of the seventh month.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה and חזקיה were twins. One was fully formed at the end of nine months, and the other was fully formed at the beginning of the seventh month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next story. It explains how unusual and difficult the births of these twins were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the twins were formed at different times, they were born separately, about two months apart. This explains why their mother יהודית suffered so much in childbirth, which matters in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: His form was completed; the baby was fully developed
At the beginning of the seventh month

phrases.english: Yehuda and Ḥizkiyya were twins,
phrases.notes: These are רבי חייא's sons. You'll see why that matters in the next story.

phrases.english: one was fully formed at the end of nine months,
and one was fully formed at the beginning of the seventh month.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהוּדָה וְחִזְקִיָּה תְּאוֹמִים הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the cases of רבי אמי and רב נחמן, the גמרא turns to a story in רבי חייא's home. This step gives the background.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The twins יהודה and חזקיה were formed and born at different times, so the births were unusual and difficult.

steps.title: יהודית asks רבי חייא and drinks a sterility potion
steps.stepSummary: יהודית, in great pain from childbirth, disguises herself and asks רבי חייא whether a woman is commanded in פריה ורביה. He says no, so she drinks a potion that makes her unable to have children.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודית, the wife of רבי חייא, had great pain in childbirth. She changed her clothes and came before רבי חייא. She asked: Is a woman commanded in פריה ורביה? He said to her: No. She went and drank a potion that prevents pregnancy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story where רבי חייא rules that a woman is not commanded in פריה ורביה. This supports that view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא gives a clear ruling: a woman is not commanded in פריה ורביה. יהודית acts on that answer and makes herself unable to have more children. The story fits the תנא קמא's view in the משנה that only the man is commanded.

keyTerms.meaning: She changed her clothes, so he would not recognize her
A potion that makes a person unable to have children

steps.confusionAlert: רבי חייא did not know he was answering his own wife. He was ruling on the general question. That is why the story counts as a real ruling.

phrases.english: Yehudit, the wife of Rabbi Ḥiyya,
had pain in childbirth.
She changed her clothes,
phrases.notes: She disguised herself so רבי חייא wouldn't realize it was his own wife asking.

phrases.english: and came before Rabbi Ḥiyya.
She said: Is a woman commanded in being fruitful and multiplying?
He said to her: No.
She went and drank a potion that causes sterility.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהוּדִית, דְּבֵיתְהוּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the background of the hard twin births and shows יהודית acting on רבי חייא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That a woman is not commanded in פריה ורביה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא's direct answer 'לא' to the question, and יהודית relying on it in practice.

steps.title: רבי חייא wishes for one more set of twins
steps.stepSummary: When the truth came out, רבי חייא told יהודית he wished she had given him one more set of twins, because his twins turned out so special: יהודה and חזקיה, and פזי and טוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, the matter became known. He said to her: If only you had given birth to one more 'belly' for me. As the Master said: יהודה and חזקיה were brothers, and פזי and טוי [were sisters].
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רבי חייא's reaction. He does not take back his ruling. He only wishes they could have had more children like the ones they had.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא's halachic answer stands. His words are personal regret, not a new ruling. The גמרא quotes a teaching about his children to show why he valued them so much, and that quote continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter was revealed; the truth came out
Belly; here a pregnancy, meaning another set of twins

steps.whatToRemember: This story fits the view that a woman is not commanded in פריה ורביה. רבי חייא ruled that way even though he personally wanted more children.

phrases.english: In the end the matter was revealed.
He said to her: If only you had given birth for me
to one more belly,
phrases.notes: He means one more pregnancy, which for her meant another set of twins.

phrases.english: as the Master said: Yehuda and Ḥizkiyya were brothers,
Pazi and Tavi
phrases.notes: These are רבי חייא's twin daughters. The sentence continues right after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְסוֹף אִיגַּלַּאי מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story of יהודית with רבי חייא's reaction once he learned what she had done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא regrets losing more children but does not take back his ruling. He praises his twin children.
